exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
cohort: The study included 16 women who experienced Post Partum Haemorrhage (PPH) out of 281 total deliveries at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Postpartum haemorrhage progresses rapidly, is easily overlooked, and significantly contributes to maternal mortality and morbidity, thus requiring crucial prediction, early recognition, and intervention.
mod_finding: The study observed that 56.25% of women with PPH had normal vaginal deliveries and 43.75% underwent caesarean section, with atonic PPH management varying between these groups.
